### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-organization.page.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via MEMBERSHIP_REACH (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-organization.page.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d19a65fe5e9dda099408514a7ad417e5f53a6f32` — the merge of head `dde114aba6539f8456d6bce0a6f8b988e96aff62` into base `d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d19a65fe5e9dda099408514a7ad417e5f53a6f32 && git checkout d19a65fe5e9dda099408514a7ad417e5f53a6f32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e dde114aba6539f8456d6bce0a6f8b988e96aff62 && git checkout -B drift-repro d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e && git merge --no-ff dde114aba6539f8456d6bce0a6f8b988e96aff62

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d8e11b58e784bb7c2208e3533ab4710921012b1e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dde114aba6539f8456d6bce0a6f8b988e96aff62`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/membership-reach.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (`:31`, `:1508`, `:2174`), packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts (`mapMembershipRole`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/membership-reach-table.test.ts, better-auth 1.7.3 (the version `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json` pins exactly; this checkout carries no `node_modules`, so the vendor was read at tag `v1.7.3`: `plugins/organization/access/statement.ts`, `routes/crud-org.ts`, `permission.ts`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`:1414`–`:1430`, the `positions` projection), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization-rename-action.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/org-record-admin-reach.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/references/ui/action.mdx, both `.changeset/24384-*.md`, packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-organization.page.ts (comment only), and objectui `2ec9e2a` `expressionUser.ts` / `ExpressionProvider.tsx` / `ActionEngine.ts` (the console's `current_user` binding). Base: merge-base `584b4225e` with `origin/main`; net diff 9 files, +288/−11. Check-runs on the head at the last read: 40, of which 34 success, 5 skipped, 1 in progress (`Test Core (3/6)`), none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

**The two reach rows — right.** better-auth 1.7.3 `access/statement.ts`: `ownerAc` carries `organization: ["update", "delete"]`, `adminAc` carries `organization: ["update"]`, `memberAc` carries `organization: []`; plugin-auth's `delegated_admin` is a member's statements plus `invitation: ['create']` (auth-manager `:3415`), so it carries no `organization:*`. `routes/crud-org.ts`: `/organization/update` checks `hasPermission({ permissions: { organization: ["update"] }, role: member.role })` and refuses with `YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_UPDATE_THIS_ORGANIZATION`; `/organization/delete` checks `organization: ["delete"]` and refuses with `YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_DELETE_THIS_ORGANIZATION`. So `update_organization` = endpoint `/organization/update`, statement `organization:update`, grades `OWNER_ADMIN`; `delete_organization` = `/organization/delete`, `organization:delete`, `[owner]` — each endpoint, statement and grade set is exactly what the door enforces. Neither route passes `allowCreatorAllPermissions`, so the owner is admitted by statement, as the table reads it. plugin-auth's `membership-reach-table.test.ts` iterates `Object.entries(MEMBERSHIP_REACH)` with no edit: for each row it requires a pathed vendor endpoint whose slice checks exactly the row's statement, and recomputes the admitted grades through the vendor's own `authorize`; 3 fixed tests + 12 rows × 2 = the 27 the dev reports. The dogfood door probes agree (member update 403, admin and owner 200 with the name changed; member and admin delete 403 with the row still there, owner 200 with the row gone). A comma-joined role is handled as the existing rows handle it: `resolve-authz-context.ts:1425` splits `m.role` on `,` and maps each part, and better-auth's `hasPermissionFn` splits on `,` and admits if any part authorizes, so `admin,member` is both offered and admitted. A role outside the closed vocabulary (ADR-0108 D1) passes through `mapMembershipRole` unchanged, so it is neither `org_owner` nor `org_admin` and the button is hidden; the vendor looks it up in `acRoles`, finds nothing, and refuses — hidden and refused agree.

**The enum — derived, not hand-listed.** `MEMBERSHIP_REACH_NAMES = Object.keys(MEMBERSHIP_REACH)` (`membership-reach.ts:165`) feeds `z.enum(MEMBERSHIP_REACH_NAMES)` on `ActionSchema` (`action.zod.ts:1508`). The only hand-written copies of the name set are pins by design (the `platform-objects.test.ts` matrix, the dogfood `EXPECTED` sets) and CHANGELOG prose; the metadata-forms translations carry label and help text only. The generated `action.mdx` is consistent: the row shows the first eight names and `+4 more` (12 = 10 + 2), and the enumerated list appends `update_organization` and `delete_organization` in `Object.keys` order.

**The lowered predicates — right, within the ruled mechanism.** `ActionSchema` lowers `lowerRequiresFeature(lowerRequiresMembershipReach(data, ctx), ctx)` (`action.zod.ts:2174`), so the grade term leads and `multiOrgEnabled` (`default-on`, `!= false`) is appended as `(GRADE-TERM) && features.multiOrgEnabled != false`. None of the three actions has an authored `visible`, so the loud-error arms do not fire. Served bytes: `update_organization` and `rename_organization` → `('org_owner' in current_user.positions || 'org_admin' in current_user.positions) && features.multiOrgEnabled != false`; `delete_organization` → `('org_owner' in current_user.positions) && features.multiOrgEnabled != false`. The matrix rows (`ADMINS && MULTI_ORG`, `(OWNER) && MULTI_ORG`) and the rename pin (`(membershipReachPredicate('update_organization')) && featureGatePredicate('multiOrgEnabled')`, equal for rename and update) spell exactly those bytes. Placement does not change the verdict: objectui's `ActionEngine.getActionsForLocation` evaluates the same `visible` against the same runner context for `list_item` and `record_header`, the predicate reads no `record.*`, and `ExpressionProvider` binds one subject as `current_user` with `positions: user.positions ?? []`, so a session face with no `positions` entry evaluates to false (hidden) rather than faulting. An owner with no active organisation gets every membership's grade projected (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1414`–`:1418`), so `org_owner` is present and the buttons are offered. **One boundary, inherited, named under ③:** `positions` are projected from the ACTIVE organisation's membership alone (`:1414`, by design: "a role held in one organization must not grant its capabilities while the caller operates in another"), while both doors look the member up in the request's `organizationId` — the record's row (`crud-org.ts` update `:50`–`:61`, delete `:40`–`:50`). For a principal whose grade differs between the active organisation and the record's, the button and the door can disagree in either direction. Within the active organisation — the case the card describes and the dogfood measures — no grade the door accepts is denied the button and no grade it refuses is offered it.

**Unchanged actions — truly unchanged.** The hunks touch `update_organization` (`:103`), `delete_organization` (`:124`) and `rename_organization` (`:250`) with one key each plus comments, and a comment line on `leave_organization`. `change_slug`, `invite_user`, `set_active_organization` and `create_organization` have no hunk; the matrix keeps `MULTI_ORG` alone for create, set-active, leave and `change_slug`, and the dogfood holds `create`, `set_active`, `leave` in `EVERY_GRADE` and asserts the served set is `ALL + UNDECIDED` for every grade.

**The dogfood pins — real controls.** The expected sets are written out per grade (`EXPECTED.owner = ALL`, `admin = EVERY_GRADE + INVITE + UPDATE`, `member = EVERY_GRADE`); the per-grade assertion compares the offered subset of `ALL` to the expected subset, so both halves (offered and not offered) are asserted; the served `visible` is required to be identical across grades before evaluation; the doors are called with effect checks on the row; `change_slug` is held out by name (`UNDECIDED`) from the graded set and from the door probe, and its presence in the served set is still asserted. The "before" (4 of 7 red on a dist built from `1eae21f`) is the dev's run, not in the tree; the in-tree control is ablation 1 (gate deleted → the matrix row and two dogfood cases red), read here as the report states it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — exact: the `requiresMembershipReach` accept set widens by two names and the exported table gains two rows; no row, name or lowering changes. `@objectstack/platform-objects` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — over-declared, not wrong: the diff widens no accept set and enlarges no public face of that package; it narrows the offered set to the door, which is a fix, and the identical shape (#21795's gates on `sys_member`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_team`) shipped as a 17.7.0 **patch** (`packages/platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md` `:1256`/`:1527`, entry `607463d`) while the spec rows shipped as a 17.7.0 minor. The dev mirrored the claim's single PR-level line into both changesets, as os-dev `:280` instructs; a minor where a patch would do breaks no consumer and `Check Changeset` is green. Not blocking; the seat may leave it. The PR body's line opens `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — the token is first after the colon and the arm is from the closed pair, so `clause2-line.mjs` reads it as a widening and ignores the tail by design (#13914's control shape). The tail's "and possibly a feature key" is now false: `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts` is not in the net diff (touched in `2eaee0cc`, restored in `dd87e1cb`). A stale parenthetical the reader does not read does not block; the seat should trim it to "the published reach table gains two rows, while the console offers fewer actions" on the next body edit, which moves no head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-organisation grade (escalate as a finding, not a blocker).** Named under ①: `positions` are active-organisation scoped and the doors are record scoped. On the organisation list and on another organisation's record page, a principal who is owner of organisation A and member of B, active in A, is offered Edit, Rename and Delete on B's row (the door refuses); active in B, they are offered none on A's row (the door admits). The second direction is new relative to `main` for these three actions, but it is the same mechanism `invite_user` on this object has carried since 17.7.0 (ruling 6228318638) and every one of the ten existing rows: ADR-0108 D1 puts the grade in `current_user.positions` and the card asked for exactly `invite_user`'s shape. The remedy on the page is one click of the ungated `set_active_organization`. The seat should file it as a finding on the reach mechanism (a record-scoped grade term, or a projection of grades per accessible organisation), not re-open this PR.
- **`Fixes #24318` dropped.** os-dev `:281` forbids `Fixes` on a card that needs a decision and `:284` prescribes the wording `#NNN remains open`; the dispatch's "Fixes both" was written before the measurement. The seat's release 6255698861 ratified it (`pm:blocked` behind #24400). `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are both green. Right.
- **Primary checkout detached.** Reported with its reading (`1eae21f`, no unique commits, the os-dev `:97` check); no edit was made on the shared tree, the worktree was then created from `origin/main` per os-dev `:26`. Housekeeping for that container, no bearing on the diff.
- **B-now pushed, then reverted.** `2eaee0cc` and `830973d1` removed `change_slug`, its i18n bundles and a `public-auth-features.ts` consumer line; `dd87e1cb` restored them. The net diff against the merge-base is nine files, and `change_slug`, the bundles and `public-auth-features.ts` are byte-identical to `main`. The PR squashes; the release comment names the history. Accepted.
- **Throwaway probe test.** `zz-probe-attach` appears in no commit on the branch (`git log --all --diff-filter=A`); its measurement is carried by #24400's body. Accepted.
- **Trailers.** All seven non-merge commits end with `Claude-Session:` and the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair AGENTS.md `:460`–`:464` requires; the harness reminder yields by the exemption named there. The merge commit `dde114aba` carries the default `git merge` message and no pair; `main` is squash-merged, so it never lands. Accepted.
- **Eight pushes.** os-dev `:30` requires the empty-branch push first, `:101` a push per compilable step, and `:57`/`:61` count `git push` as one stroke outside the REST budget. Right.
- **Ablation 1 on an intermediate tree.** It ran while `change_slug` was removed; the mutated line (`requiresMembershipReach: 'delete_organization'`, `:124`) is identical on the final head and the two reds it produced depend on nothing `change_slug` touches. A control not re-run on the final head is weaker evidence; read-only here, recorded as claimed. Ablation 2 ran on the final tree.
- **Open question 1 (the `change_slug` shape).** Answered by the seat as B behind #24400 (release 6255698861). For this PR the right act was to change nothing, and that is what shipped: `change_slug` keeps `requiresFeature: 'multiOrgEnabled'` alone, its target and location, and the dogfood pins its presence while holding it out of the graded set by name.
- **Open question 2 (a reach term for `change_slug` meanwhile).** The dev's "No" is right: its door is cloud's `org-admin` (`cloud-route-authz.ts` `callerCanRenameOrg`), outside better-auth; `membership-reach-table.test.ts` requires every row's endpoint to be a pathed vendor HTTP door, so a `change_slug` row would turn that test red, and reusing `update_organization`'s row would book a non-vendor door under a vendor statement. The grade belongs to whichever shape #24318 takes.
- **Out-of-scope finding (#24400).** Class (b) as filed: `ObjectExtensionSchema.guidance.actions` (`object.zod.ts`) promises that a top-level action with `objectName` is attached by `defineStack()`, and `mergeActionsIntoObjects` (`stack.zod.ts`) attaches only within the same stack, measured on a booted showcase. Correctly filed, not a claim, and it is shape B's prerequisite; triage owns grade and lane. The second entry ("carrier: #24318's decision, noted, not filed") is discharged by the release comment.
- Nothing in the diff changes a door, adds an error code, or gates `leave_organization`, as the claim forbade.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24384-org-admin-actions-reach`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
